name: ISIS Neutron and Muon Source
notes: Created by the accelerator-neutrino-historical lead solely to host the placement of experiment:karmen; this record does not attempt full coverage of ISIS's neutron/muon science programme.

ISIS is a pulsed spallation neutron and muon source at the Rutherford Appleton Laboratory operated by STFC; KARMEN used its 800 MeV proton beam stop as a neutrino source (see src:karmen-prc-1998-nue-nutau-limits: 'the beam stop neutrino source ISIS').

operator.quote: located at the Rutherford Appleton Laboratory in Oxfordshire, UK, and operated by the Science and Technology Facilities Council.

summary.plain: A pulsed particle accelerator facility in Oxfordshire, England, that fires protons at a heavy-metal target to make neutrons and muons for materials research. In the 1990s its proton beam stop also served as a source of neutrinos for the KARMEN experiment.
summary.technical: STFC-operated pulsed spallation neutron and muon source at the Rutherford Appleton Laboratory, Harwell Campus, Didcot, Oxfordshire, using an 800 MeV proton synchrotron; its beam stop supplied stopped-pion/muon-decay neutrinos to the KARMEN experiment from 1990 to 2001.
